input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: Calling `.strip()` also removes intentional whitespace from the prompt, including the space after the default `": "` suffix. ANSI removal should preserve the remaining text.
- rationale: When stdout is redirected or otherwise does not support ANSI, a normal prompt such as `"Name: "` reaches this branch and becomes `"Name:"`. Users see input or captured output run directly against the colon, and any intentional leading whitespace is also lost, even when the prompt contains no ANSI codes.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. In the non-color branch, the extra .strip() after ANSI removal drops the trailing space from "Name: ", so the prompt shows as "Name:" when output is redirected.
